text:
The Predators have won five straight, outscoring teams 18-8, and this run is better than the season around it. They got 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those games. Across the season it's 50%, and at five on five only 46%. The difference has been Juuse Saros, who has stopped .937 over his last five starts. Nashville's goalies have allowed almost ten fewer goals than expected, and our numbers have the Preds about three and a half points ahead of what they deserved at 9-4-5.

The front office is still reshaping the roster. Nashville sent Matthew Wood to Seattle for Shane Wright, and Wright fit in right away beside Filip Forsberg, who keeps piling up assists. The old guard is doing its part: Steven Stamkos moved into the all-time top five in power-play goals, and Roman Josi is a point from 800 with Norris chatter and, inevitably, trade rumors attached.

The worry is the middle of the lineup. Mavrik Bourque has 2 points in his last 10 against 4.9 expected, and the Stamkos and Ryan O'Reilly line isn't winning its minutes. The Brady Skjei and Nick Perbix pair gets only 43% of the chances. The best line has been the grinders: Ross Colton, Jack Drury and Adam Edstrom.

The playoff odds are 64% in our simulations. What to watch: whether Saros can carry this while the five-on-five play catches up.
headline: Nashville is winning on Saros and a hot week
